prelude: Outbreak of Orrin flu. The 4 people in a start-up office (Petra, Tomas, Sofia, and Chloe) have these close contacts: Petra-Sofia, Petra-Chloe, Tomas-Chloe, and Sofia-Chloe. On each day, every infectious person passes Orrin flu to each susceptible contact independently with probability 65 percent; at the end of each day, each person who was infectious at the start of that day recovers (becomes immune) with probability 40 percent. Someone infected during a day becomes infectious from the next day on. On day 0 exactly one of them, equally likely to be any of the 4, came back infectious; 2 days have passed since. An antibody test detects past or current infection with probability 80 percent and gives a false positive for someone never infected with probability 10 percent. A swab test detects current infectiousness with probability 75 percent and is falsely positive with probability 6 percent for anyone not currently infectious. Test results are independent given everyone's true status.
